PS5 DualSense Controller Test: Buttons, Sticks & Triggers

By PadLab · Updated October 9, 2026

Use PadLab to inspect the inputs your PS5 DualSense or DualSense Edge exposes to the browser. This is a quick button, stick, trigger and connection check—not a firmware calibration utility.

Start controller test →

Run a DualSense test

  1. Connect with a USB data cable or pair through Bluetooth.
  2. Open the PadLab tester and press a button while the page is focused.
  3. Press Cross, Circle, Square, Triangle, the D-pad, bumpers, Options, Create and both stick clicks.
  4. Squeeze L2 and R2 gradually, then release both sticks and run the drift sample.

What PadLab can see

PadLab can display browser-exposed buttons, axes, standard mapping and supported vibration. DualSense-specific features such as adaptive trigger resistance, touchpad gestures, light-bar state, microphone status and every advanced haptic mode may not be exposed through the standard Gamepad API.

DualSense drift and center offset

Leave both sticks untouched and use the three-second drift test. Review mean and peak radial offset, then compare that observation with the deadzone used by your game. A small nonzero center value is not a universal failure threshold.

Read how stick drift and deadzones work.

If the controller is missing

Use a known data cable, keep the page visible, press a physical button, and check whether the controller is connected to another device. See controller detection troubleshooting.

USB or Bluetooth: isolate one connection at a time

Start with a USB data cable so pairing is not another variable. To pair over Bluetooth, disconnect USB and follow Sony’s instructions: with the controller off, hold Create and PS until the light bar blinks, then select the controller in your device’s Bluetooth settings. Return to PadLab and press a controller button.

Record the connection used for each test. A successful USB result does not establish Bluetooth support, and a game’s native DualSense features do not establish browser support.

Read the controls by position

Physical controlStandard browser inputWhat to inspect
Cross / Circle / Square / TriangleButtons 0 / 1 / 2 / 3Each press should affect the expected cell and release again.
L2 / R2Buttons 6 / 7Compare released, partly squeezed and fully squeezed values.
Left / right stickAxes 0–1 / 2–3Check both directions and the resting offset.

These indices apply only when the browser reports a standard mapping. The Create button is the PS5 sharing control; labels inherited from older PlayStation layouts may say Share. Follow observed input numbers if the layout is unmapped.

When a feature appears missing

A trigger value tests the reported input, not adaptive resistance. A vibration command does not certify advanced haptics. For a missing face button, compare the button routine before assuming a fault. If USB works but Bluetooth does not, repeat pairing and check the exact operating-system support listed by Sony.
